seal.statement: The whole corpus is a fact about an immutable commit, but the post-push canary could only learn it from one place: a proof-scope artifact uploaded by the ci gate run. On 0f93df70c the ci gate refused before writing one (RELEASE_PROOF_REQUIRED for a package-lock devDependency removal), so the canary re-proved all 2127 files - 74 minutes - for a corpus the local push gate had already proved green on that exact sha. The proof authority already keys durable receipts by commit (refs/lagrange-proofs/<contract>/<sha>) but held one contract, read only by the release path. This quest registers corpus-full-v1, has the push gate record it when its own whole-corpus run passes, and gives the canary's decision one witnessed owner (scripts/checks/canary-corpus-needed.js) that accepts either proof: the gate run's scope for this sha, or a durable receipt for this sha. Anything unknown, unreadable or non-boolean leaves the corpus owed, because a canary that runs needlessly costs time while one that skips wrongly costs the proof. The authority is spawned rather than imported so the gate's import closure keeps tripping its own full-corpus triggers.

text: corpus-full-v1 registered in the proof authority with a resolveCorpusProof lookup; the push gate records it (spawned CLI, best effort) after a green whole-corpus run; new witnessed owner scripts/checks/canary-corpus-needed.js decides from the gate scope or a durable receipt, fail-open to owed; the canary decide job calls it with --sha/--scope/--remote and only needed= reaches the step output

round 1 REJECT (3 blocking): B1 resolveCorpusProof delegated to resolveProof whose identity rung let a sibling commit's receipt answer - proven in a fixture: a CHANGELOG-only commit read as proven, and release-notes.test.js reads the real CHANGELOG while neither CHANGELOG.md nor package.json is a full-corpus trigger; B2 the recording seam (runDecision) was unexported and unwitnessed, so recording after a cone proof stayed green under mutation; B3 the new checkout in the decide job deletes a workspace-relative download-artifact path, so the scope proof was dead in production. Non-blocking: job condition == 'true' skipped the corpus on a failed decide; a manual dirty-tree run could mint a receipt; the own-property guard was unwitnessed; workflow_dispatch lost its override; no timeout on the spawned record. Closure and fail-open matrix (~50 hostile inputs) verified sound.

round 1 repairs: contracts declare identityReuse (release-full yes, corpus-full no) so resolveProof skips the identity rung and recordProof publishes no identity ref for the corpus - witnessed twice, by a sibling-commit fixture and by a git spy proving the rung is never taken; runDecision exported with injected runners and witnessed (cone records nothing, red corpus records nothing, green corpus records once for its own head); recordCorpusProof refuses unless HEAD is the sha and the tree is clean, with a 60 s timeout; the workflow checks out BEFORE downloading the scope to runner.temp, the corpus job is gated on needed != 'false' plus decide not skipped, and a hand dispatch passes --force; five new receipts (11 total)

round 2 REJECT (1 blocking, B4, introduced by the round-1 repair): the new runDecision witness called the real writeProofScope with the real head, and this test file is in the safety spine, so every change proof left test-output/proof-scope.json saying {sha: <head>, fullCorpus: true}; ci uploads that file as the proof-scope artifact after the step, so the canary would have skipped the corpus on every push - the exact outcome the quest exists to prevent, unmasked by the B3 fix. Confirmed fixed at the contract for B1 (no corpus identity ref minted, release reuse intact), B2 and B3; mutation matrix 12/12 red including the two green in round 1; fail-open matrix ~45 cases with no wrong skips; closure, hygiene and probe-step guarantees intact. Non-blocking: always() should be !cancelled(); treeIsCommit ignored untracked files; indexProof has no identityReuse guard.

round 2 repair: runDecision injects the scope WRITER too, so the spine witness cannot stamp the artifact ci uploads; the witness asserts test-output/proof-scope.json is byte-identical before and after (and the mutation that restores the real writer reproduces the poisoning); treeIsCommit now counts untracked files (ignored artifacts are not listed by --porcelain); the corpus job uses !cancelled() so a superseded run cannot launch the 300-minute job; writeProofScope's doc names the artifact and warns tests off the real root

round 3 APPROVE: B4 fixed with two independent teeth - the byte comparison AND the injected-writer assertion, so a pre-seeded stale scope file cannot defeat it (verifier pre-seeded the exact poisoned bytes and the witness still went red); mutation matrix 16/17 red at review time, every safety branch and both identity guards; NB2 checked empirically against the gate's real workspace injections (GATE_WORKSPACE_DIRECTORIES node_modules+data, /data/* ignored with three existing negations) - status --porcelain is clean before and after injections, so the receipt will actually mint; B1 re-verified per contract with the release identity path intact; fail-open and force matrices ~50 cases with no wrong skips; closure 26 modules without the authority; hygiene and probe-step guarantees intact. Remaining non-blocking left as records: indexProof has no identityReuse guard (a ref the lookup cannot read), --force typo tolerance, refs/lagrange-proofs pruning owner (should cover release refs too), and NB3 a corpus run that dirties a tracked file simply re-proves.
round 3 follow-up: the tree-guard spy now pins the git arguments, so reverting to --untracked-files=no turns the witness red (verifier mutation n, the one green case at review time)

the sealed probe is immutable: widening doneWhen from 6 to 11 required receipts after start refused the land. Restored the sealed six; the five receipts added in rounds 2-3 (sibling identity, no identity rung, hand dispatch, only-a-green-corpus-records, tree-must-be-the-commit) remain in the harness and the receipt file as evidence beyond the probe, and the log carries them.

Altitude check after three verifier rounds. The altitude is right and the rounds proved it: every defect was at a seam, and each was fixed where the seam lives rather than at the call site - identity reuse became a property of the CONTRACT (so the release path keeps it and the corpus cannot have it), the recording decision became an injectable seam in runDecision (so a cone proof provably records nothing), and the artifact-versus-checkout ordering was fixed in the workflow. The one repair that went wrong, B4, is the lesson: my own witness called the real writeProofScope, and because this test file is in the safety spine it would have stamped fullCorpus:true into the artifact ci uploads on every push, turning the canary off for ever. A witness that touches production state is not a witness. That is why every effect in the seam is injected now and the witness asserts the real artifact is untouched, with two independent teeth so a stale file cannot defeat it. No scope change is warranted: the quest stays the decision owner plus the receipt contract, and the four follow-ups it surfaced (refs pruning, indexProof guard, runner output bound, artifact retention) are separate owners and recorded as such.

the corpus-job condition is pinned in a second place: test/release/project-hardening-contracts.test.js asserted the old == 'true' string.
